## Motivation

The GLM-5.3-Flash k-pool indexer selects its top-k pooled groups with `kpool_topk_transform`, which runs one thread block per row. At decode time there is one row per request, so a single block scans the whole pooled history while the rest of the GPU idles. At 1M context this costs about 84 us per DSA layer per decode step, which is most of the decode slowdown from short to long context.

The top-k v2 kernel already splits long rows across thread-block clusters. This PR routes the k-pool indexer through it, with pool expansion, tail append and the output transform fused into the same kernel.

## Modifications

- **Fused k-pool mode in top-k v2** (`TopKMode::KPOOL`, `transform_kpool`): selection over pooled scores plus pool expansion, tail append and page-table or offset mapping in one launch, on every dispatch route (register, streaming, cluster, persistent cluster). The launch dispatch is shared with `transform_paged` through `launch<kMode>()`.
- **Ragged k-pool entry point** (`transform_kpool_ragged`): per-row windows (`row_starts`, `page_table_row_index`) for prefill and for any caller without a plan. Its select-then-transform body is shared with the ROCm `topk_packed_kernel` through `ragged_select_transform`.
- **Plans live in metadata**: decode and verify metadata build the top-k v2 plan once per forward, before the logits kernel, and refresh it on CUDA-graph replay. Rows without a matching plan take the ragged path.
- `topk_from_pooled_history_logits` dispatches to the planned path, then the ragged path, then the existing kernels. `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` keeps the existing kernels.

## Accuracy Tests

- Kernel parity against the existing fused kernel: every output mode (no transform, page table, page table with row index, offsets), with and without tail columns, aligned and unaligned `row_starts`, short and zero-length rows. All selections match, up to exact score ties at the cut-off.
- CUDA-graph replay with the plan refreshed between replays, batch 1 to 300, covering every cluster dispatch route including the persistent cluster: 0 mismatches.
- GSM8K with `sgl-eval run gsm8k --max-tokens 16384 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95` (1319 questions), GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on B300 with the cookbook commands:

| Configuration | main | this PR | Eval time main | Eval time this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High Throughput | 97.04% | 96.89% | 1m 55s | 1m 55s |
| Low Latency (MTP 5/1/6) | 97.12% | 96.89% | 1m 37s | 1m 28s |

Both gaps are 2 to 3 questions, within run-to-run spread at temperature 1.0. GSM8K sequences mostly stay below the 2048-token top-k budget, so this run validates the metadata, plan and transform path end to end.

- Long-context selection with `sgl-eval run ruler2 --max-tokens 16384 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95` (all 12 subtasks, the same generated datasets on both servers), High Throughput cookbook command. Score is the RULER2 headline; the family columns average the four multi-key NIAH, four multi-value NIAH and four QA subtasks:

| Context | Samples | Score main | Score this PR | MK-NIAH main / PR | MV-NIAH main / PR | QA main / PR | Eval time main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | 300 | 86.63% | 88.41% | 93.0 / 95.0 | 79.9 / 79.2 | 87.0 / 91.0 | 21m 0s / 18m 44s |
| 512K | 120 | 79.12% | 77.66% | 92.4 / 92.5 | 54.9 / 53.0 | 90.0 / 87.5 | 28m 5s / 25m 50s |
| 1M | 60 | 72.72% | 72.94% | 95.0 / 85.1 | 23.2 / 43.7 | 100.0 / 90.0 | 27m 55s / 26m 48s |

The headline differences change sign across lengths and stay within sampling noise (about 2 points at 128K and 3.5 points at 512K). At 1M each subtask has 5 samples, so family averages move by up to 20 points per sample in both directions. Error rate is 0% and truncation at most 3.3% on every run.

Eval times are the wall-clock time of each `sgl-eval` run (256 concurrent requests for GSM8K; 16 for RULER2 at 128K and 512K, 8 at 1M). In total the accuracy evals took 2h 35m: GSM8K 6m 55s (four runs), RULER2 1h 17m on main and 1h 11m on this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Top-k op on B300, GLM-5.3-Flash shapes (`index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4).

Decode (CUDA graph, score width fixed at 1M context, time per call in us). Scores are written by the logits kernel immediately before top-k, so the L2-hot measurement matches serving:

| Batch \ context | 4K | 32K | 131K | 262K | 1M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.7 -> 2.8 | 9.1 -> 4.1 | 14.9 -> 7.2 | 30.3 -> 7.5 | 83.3 -> 8.9 |
| 8 | 6.9 -> 3.2 | 9.3 -> 4.3 | 15.2 -> 7.6 | 30.9 -> 8.2 | 83.0 -> 11.2 |
| 32 | 6.7 -> 3.7 | 9.7 -> 5.4 | 15.4 -> 10.7 | 30.9 -> 11.3 | 83.5 -> 16.0 |
| 128 | 7.1 -> 4.8 | 10.3 -> 6.1 | 16.2 -> 10.9 | 31.7 -> 15.6 | 160.4 -> 82.4 |

Prefill (ragged path, causal rows ending at the given context, time per call in us; the score buffer far exceeds L2):

| Rows | Context | main | this PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1M | 2429.2 | 1298.5 | 1.87x |
| 4096 | 262K | 598.4 | 333.6 | 1.79x |
| 16384 | 65K | 881.5 | 480.6 | 1.83x |
| 16384 | 16K | 450.8 | 241.9 | 1.86x |
| 2048 | 8K | 62.1 | 33.1 | 1.87x |

End to end, `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server` at batch 1 with 256 output tokens (cache flushed per case), High Throughput cookbook command on B300. Each sweep ran three times per server; the first pass includes one-time JIT compilation, so the table is the mean of passes 2 and 3:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 0.214 | 0.214 | 4.68 | 4.61 |

| 512K | 10.530 | 10.178 | 5.17 | 4.76 |
| 1M | 24.917 | 23.240 | 5.66 | 4.86 |

Reviewed c31b9b1. One correctness concern with threshold-bin overflow in the newly enabled cluster k-pool path; details and a targeted regression probe are inline.

Could we handle threshold-bin overflow before enabling the cluster path for k-pool?

This launch newly routes long k-pool rows through `TopKCluster`, which [still truncates an overflowing threshold bin](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/topk_impl.cuh#L847-L850). It retains at most `kMaxNumTie = 2048` candidates in arrival order, then selects from that subset. If the bucket contains distinct FP32 scores, this can discard genuinely higher-scoring pools, rather than just reorder equal-score ties.

The [existing k-pool selector rescans overfull bins using exact keys](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/kpool_topk_transform.cuh#L130-L186), so enabling this dispatch introduces a selection-correctness regression for those inputs. Register/streaming v2 already have overflow refinement; cluster does not.

A targeted case is batch 1, 65536 pools, pool size 4, and 512 selected pools, with shuffled scores `1 + i * 2**-23`. All 65536 scores are distinct FP32 values but map to the same 10-bit coarse bucket. That exceeds the candidate buffer even though the requested top-k fits.

<details>
<summary>Minimal regression probe for a cluster-capable H100/B200/B300</summary>

```python
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk import (
    plan_topk_v2,
    topk_transform_kpool_v2,
)

torch.manual_seed(1234)
n, pool_size, group_k = 65536, 4, 512
lengths = torch.tensor([n], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
plan = plan_topk_v2(lengths)
scores = (
    1.0 + torch.randperm(n, device="cuda").float() * 2.0**-23
).view(1, n)
out = torch.empty(
    (1, group_k * pool_size), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
)

topk_transform_kpool_v2(scores, lengths, out, pool_size, plan)
groups = out[:, ::pool_size].long() // pool_size
expected = scores.topk(group_k, dim=1).indices

torch.testing.assert_close(
    groups.sort(dim=1).values,
    expected.sort(dim=1).values,
    atol=0,
    rtol=0,
)
```

The device must have schedulable clusters; a single-block fallback would mask the issue. I verified the single-bucket input condition on CPU, but have **not run this probe on a GPU**, so I do not have a measured mismatch count.

</details>

The existing narrow-distribution v2 test [explicitly skips possible cluster shapes](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py#L382-L397), and the k-pool overfull-bin test calls the legacy kernel directly. Could we add coverage through the new planned entry point, comparing it with the legacy/ragged paths, and either refine overflowing cluster bins or fall back to an exact path?

Thanks, confirmed: your probe got 511/512 wrong pools on B300. Every `TopKCluster` user truncated the bin, not just k-pool. As you noted, #37625 doesn't cover v2.

Fixed in f194e3dc66, 197403d186 and 80be160f73 with an exact fallback. An overflowing row is now redone by the existing `Streaming` selector (exact since #37941): `topk_main_kernel` does it for persistent rows, and rank 0 does it for small-batch rows. Refining inside the cluster cost the persistent kernel 6–12% even when it never ran, so I kept that path unchanged. Normal scores stay within ~1% on most shapes, with up to ~3% worst case.

Tests now cover the cluster plan: narrow-distribution v2 shapes that reach the small-batch and persistent kernels, page/dual outputs, and a planned k-pool overflow test with graph replay. They fail on the old kernel and pass now.
I don't think this is a good way to handle the overflow. For cluster path, the overflow is quite frequent. We should actually let the whole cluster to handle the overflow instead of delaying it.

@DarkSharpness I tried that first actually, it cost the persistent kernel 6-12% on normal rows even when it never ran, so deferring was on purpose.

How frequent are you seeing it, and on what? On randn it never overflows for me. And if it's common, hasn't cluster been giving wrong top-k all along (DSV4 too)? Would a finer coarse histogram so it rarely overflows work for you?

the "wrong" here is very tricky. as far as I know, the model can tolerate some kind of bias. For topk impl, even if the score itself is "wrong", the numeric value difference between wrongly selected rows and truly selected rows are small, so the expected attention score might be close.

Yeah fair, they're all in the same bin so it's more bias than wrong. I checked on B300 with real text prompts from 64K to 1M tokens. GLM-5.3-Flash k-pool never overflows (max cutoff bin 501 vs 2048), but GLM-5.3 token DSA overflows on 5% of decode rows, almost all from one indexer layer that overflows nearly every step, so this deferral would actually slow that down.

Can we just drop the overflow handling from this PR and keep the truncation like before? Then I or someone can do the whole-cluster refine in a separate PR if we want it exact
sure. let's defer the overflow handling from this PR
TODO: Add exact threshold-bin overflow handling across the whole cluster in a follow-up PR, with regression tests that exercise the cluster paths.

Could we handle threshold-bin overflow before enabling the cluster path for k-pool?

This launch newly routes long k-pool rows through `TopKCluster`, which [still truncates an overflowing threshold bin](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/topk_impl.cuh#L847-L850). It retains at most `kMaxNumTie = 2048` candidates in arrival order, then selects from that subset. If the bucket contains distinct FP32 scores, this can discard genuinely higher-scoring pools, rather than just reorder equal-score ties.

The [existing k-pool selector rescans overfull bins using exact keys](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/kpool_topk_transform.cuh#L130-L186), so enabling this dispatch introduces a selection-correctness regression for those inputs. Register/streaming v2 already have overflow refinement; cluster does not.

A targeted case is batch 1, 65536 pools, pool size 4, and 512 selected pools, with shuffled scores `1 + i * 2**-23`. All 65536 scores are distinct FP32 values but map to the same 10-bit coarse bucket. That exceeds the candidate buffer even though the requested top-k fits.

<details>
<summary>Minimal regression probe for a cluster-capable H100/B200/B300</summary>

```python
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk import (
    plan_topk_v2,
    topk_transform_kpool_v2,
)

torch.manual_seed(1234)
n, pool_size, group_k = 65536, 4, 512
lengths = torch.tensor([n], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
plan = plan_topk_v2(lengths)
scores = (
    1.0 + torch.randperm(n, device="cuda").float() * 2.0**-23
).view(1, n)
out = torch.empty(
    (1, group_k * pool_size), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
)

topk_transform_kpool_v2(scores, lengths, out, pool_size, plan)
groups = out[:, ::pool_size].long() // pool_size
expected = scores.topk(group_k, dim=1).indices

torch.testing.assert_close(
    groups.sort(dim=1).values,
    expected.sort(dim=1).values,
    atol=0,
    rtol=0,
)
```

The device must have schedulable clusters; a single-block fallback would mask the issue. I verified the single-bucket input condition on CPU, but have **not run this probe on a GPU**, so I do not have a measured mismatch count.

</details>

The existing narrow-distribution v2 test [explicitly skips possible cluster shapes](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c31b9b1efe9c0ae7539b93d2cb7ce798bf95a63c/test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py#L382-L397), and the k-pool overfull-bin test calls the legacy kernel directly. Could we add coverage through the new planned entry point, comparing it with the legacy/ragged paths, and either refine overflowing cluster bins or fall back to an exact path?

Thanks, confirmed: your probe got 511/512 wrong pools on B300. Every `TopKCluster` user truncated the bin, not just k-pool. As you noted, #37625 doesn't cover v2.

Fixed in f194e3dc66, 197403d186 and 80be160f73 with an exact fallback. An overflowing row is now redone by the existing `Streaming` selector (exact since #37941): `topk_main_kernel` does it for persistent rows, and rank 0 does it for small-batch rows. Refining inside the cluster cost the persistent kernel 6–12% even when it never ran, so I kept that path unchanged. Normal scores stay within ~1% on most shapes, with up to ~3% worst case.

Tests now cover the cluster plan: narrow-distribution v2 shapes that reach the small-batch and persistent kernels, page/dual outputs, and a planned k-pool overflow test with graph replay. They fail on the old kernel and pass now.
I don't think this is a good way to handle the overflow. For cluster path, the overflow is quite frequent. We should actually let the whole cluster to handle the overflow instead of delaying it.

@DarkSharpness I tried that first actually, it cost the persistent kernel 6-12% on normal rows even when it never ran, so deferring was on purpose.

How frequent are you seeing it, and on what? On randn it never overflows for me. And if it's common, hasn't cluster been giving wrong top-k all along (DSV4 too)? Would a finer coarse histogram so it rarely overflows work for you?

the "wrong" here is very tricky. as far as I know, the model can tolerate some kind of bias. For topk impl, even if the score itself is "wrong", the numeric value difference between wrongly selected rows and truly selected rows are small, so the expected attention score might be close.

Yeah fair, they're all in the same bin so it's more bias than wrong. I checked on B300 with real text prompts from 64K to 1M tokens. GLM-5.3-Flash k-pool never overflows (max cutoff bin 501 vs 2048), but GLM-5.3 token DSA overflows on 5% of decode rows, almost all from one indexer layer that overflows nearly every step, so this deferral would actually slow that down.

Can we just drop the overflow handling from this PR and keep the truncation like before? Then I or someone can do the whole-cluster refine in a separate PR if we want it exact
sure. let's defer the overflow handling from this PR
